detailed_description: The Tree Chart Generator creates dynamic hierarchical visualizations using orthogonal and radial tree layouts, rendering complex parent-child relationships through SVG path calculations. This tool leverages the Reingold-Tilford algorithm to generate tidy tree diagrams that optimize spatial distribution while maintaining node alignment. Developers and data analysts can input hierarchical data in JSON, CSV, or YAML formats to produce interactive charts with collapsible branches and customizable node styling. The radial layout employs polar coordinate transformations to display data in concentric circles, ideal for organizational charts or file system visualizations. Built-in support for weighted edges and conditional formatting enables semantic highlighting of critical paths. Unlike conventional chart builders, this tool implements Web Workers for client-side data processing, eliminating server latency when handling structures with thousands of nodes. The resulting visualizations maintain accessibility standards through ARIA-labeled nodes and keyboard navigation support.
usage_steps: Open the tool and select 'Create New Chart' to activate the workspace
Import hierarchical data via JSON/CSV upload, URL import, or manual entry in the Schema Builder
Choose orthogonal or radial layout using the Layout Presets panel with real-time preview
Customize node appearance in the Style Editor: modify stroke widths, apply color gradients based on depth levels, and configure label positioning
Enable interactivity features like dynamic zoom (mousewheel) and node collapse/expand (click)
Export the chart as SVG, PNG, or embeddable HTML/JS using the responsive Export dropdown with size presets
usage_examples: Mapping corporate organizational structure with 500+ employees using CSV import and departmental color coding
Visualizing server directory contents by converting Linux 'ls -R' output to interactive radial tree
Creating genealogical charts from GEDCOM data with birth/death date annotations on nodes
Debugging software dependency trees by importing package.json and highlighting version conflicts through edge thickness
